name: pcb-e5-block
title: PCB-E5 DOCK BLOCK, the raised contact board under board A's spring pins
_table_why: Board E5 had no board table at all until 17 September 2026, and three rules read 'no verdict for this board' because every tool that answers them starts from a netlist. E5 is generated by gen_pcb_e5.py from board A's own board file: it has no schematic and no netlist, and its nets are board A's, read off A's board by position under each spring pin. What it CAN do is declare, which is what this file is for. Nothing here is a chain configuration: E5 is built by build_e5.sh and not by full.sh.
_chain_why: E5 is not built by a chain: `build_e5.sh` generates it from board A's board file and there is no schematic, no netlist, no pre-router, no route and no finish. Every test that asks a board table for its chain configuration skips a table that declares this, and every test that asks it for a FACT about the board reads it like any other: the difference is what the table is for, not how much of it there is.
_external_ports_why: No conductor of this board leaves the enclosure. Every target on its face mates with a spring pin of board A a few millimetres above it, inside the sealed case, and the pack pair arrives on plated wire lands underneath from the battery module, also inside the case. The conductors that DO leave the case are board E's, at the wall receptacle, and board E declares them.
_safety_lines_why: This board carries no active part of any kind: it is copper targets, plated wire lands and mounting holes. Nothing on it can assert or read a line, so no line whose assertion inhibits a hazard lives here; SHORE_INHIBIT crosses the dock as a conductor of boards A and E and is judged on those two.
_stackup_dk_why: STK-001 RESIDUE, OWED TO THIS BOARD'S NEXT GENERATION (18 September 2026, stackup_gate's first run). The board file carries epsilon_r 4.6 on its FR-4 core where the named record for the 2L-2oz stack says 4.5. The record is right: the fabricator's own capability document states the dielectric constant per build and gives 4.5 for a two-layer board (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md), while the 4.6 in this board file came from its impedance page, which is about the multilayer cores, and was corrected in stackup_write.py on 16 September. Nothing computed on this board moves: it carries no impedance target, so the number reaches no verdict except this one. It is NOT patched into the committed board file, because rewriting a board changes its sha and stales every reading taken on it for a number that changes nothing; the next generation writes the stack from stackup_write.STACKS and carries 4.5 by construction. Until then STK-001 reads FAIL of 8 on this board and says exactly this. AND THE FOLDER IS THE DECIDING HALF ON THIS BOARD: E5 is the one board of the seven whose deliverable folder passes the final gate (21 of 21), so rewriting its board file to correct a dielectric constant that reaches no computed number would stale that folder and turn DOC-001 and DFM-001 from PASS into FAIL to take STK-001 from FAIL to PASS. That is a worse set, not a better one. The correction rides with the re-cut this board gets when the order is placed, where the folder is rebuilt anyway.
_doc002_why: DOC-002 IS ANSWERED IN THE GENERATOR AND WAITING ON THE FOLDERS, NOT ON A TOOL (19 September 2026). `doc_provenance` asks that every document asserting hardware numbers carry a `sha256` naming the artefact it was read from, and that the sha be the gerber zip in its own folder. All SEVEN boards' `ORDER-NOTES.txt` fail it and every one fails the same way, 'names no artefact'. **The generator already writes that block**: `make_handoff.py` has carried a PROVENANCE section since 12 September (the board's sha256, the gerber zip's, the date, and the sentence that nothing in the note is typed by hand). The committed notes simply predate it. So the rule needs no code and no ruling: it answers itself the moment an order set is re-cut. **What blocks the re-cut is the order table, and that is decision-bound.** Run today it REFUSES, correctly: 'the tree's newest C deliverable is C24, the table says C17, and the hand-fitted list still describes C17. An order set built now would attach C17 notes to C24 gerbers.' Bringing the table forward is cheap; bringing the FOLDERS forward is not, because A, D and E have no folder at their declared phase and cannot cut one while TRN-001 holds the finish (decision 31). E5 is the only board whose folder IS at its declared phase, which is why E5 is the only board reading FAIL here while the other six read INCONCLUSIVE: the rule is looking at the one folder it can see. Board E5's own answer is one re-cut of the order set, and it is worth taking the moment decision 31 frees the others.
_stk001_residue_why: STK-001 IS ONE LINE AND IT CANNOT BE APPLIED ALONE (19 September 2026, verified rather than assumed). The board carries `epsilon_r 4.6` in its stackup block where the 2-layer 2 oz record says **4.5**, from the fabricator's own capability page, and that is the whole disagreement: `stackup_write.py` rewritten over a copy of this board changes **exactly one line** and nothing else, and the tool is pure text with no KiCad behind it, so the edit costs a second. **What it cannot do is stand alone.** This board's deliverable folder holds it BYTE FOR BYTE (sha256 identical on both sides), which is what DFM-001 and DOC-001 read; changing the board without re-cutting the folder breaks a rule that passes today to fix one that fails, and re-cutting the folder is blocked behind decision 31 for the boards that hold the set. So the deferral of 18 September stands and now carries its reason: **the fix is a line, the obstacle is the folder**, and STK-001 closes itself in the same commit that re-cuts this board's deliverable. The number changes nothing electrically on a board with no impedance target; it is the record being true about what was built.
_board_e5_state_why: 19 September 2026 10:05 CEST, BOARD E5'S THREE FAILURES, AND TWO OF THEM ARE ONE FILE (19 of 25 verified, the highest ratio in the set). STK-001 is the epsilon_r residue: this board's stackup says 4.6 where the fabricator's capability document says 4.5, one disagreement of eight compared, deliberately NOT patched because a rewrite stales every reading on this board for a number that changes nothing on a board with no impedance target, and it is carried for the next generation. DOC-002 is ONE LINE IN ONE GENERATED FILE: `PCB-E5-BLOCK-E5/ORDER-NOTES.txt` asserts hardware numbers and names no artefact, and `make_handoff.py` has written the two provenance lines (the board's sha256 and the gerber zip's) since 13 September, so the file in the tree simply predates its own generator. THE SAME FILE ALSO CONTRADICTS RULING 7 in its own text, saying '1 oz outer copper' in the PCB block while its ASSEMBLY block says 'bare 2 oz board' and the ruling orders E5 and P at 2 oz. NEITHER IS TOUCHED HERE: rebuilding the order set is the paperwork pass OUT-001 needs, it rewrites every board's notes from folders that are stale on five of seven boards, and it is the one operation in this tree that an unattended session should not do on its own. OUT-001 is the set's. Counts are generated in v2/docs/PCB-OPEN-PAIRS.md.
